item.title: Reverse drill 2026-10-07: Kernighan bit loop
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64.
Reverse this short function to equivalent C:
```asm mystery: xor eax, eax test ecx, ecx je done again: lea edx, [rcx-1] inc eax and ecx, edx jne again done: ret ```
What does `mystery(unsigned x)` compute? What does `and ecx, edx` do each pass?
## Answer
```c int mystery(unsigned x) { int n = 0; while (x) { x &= x - 1; n++; } return n; } ```
Population count (number of set bits), Kernighan style.
## Explanation
- `lea edx,[rcx-1]` is just subtraction (no memory access); `x & (x-1)` clears the lowest set bit, so each loop pass removes exactly one 1-bit. - `and` sets ZF itself, so the `jne` needs no separate `test`; the loop ends when `x` hits 0, and the up-front `test/je` handles `x == 0` returning 0. - Iterations = number of set bits, so `mystery(0xF0F0)` = 8.
